label: lower after rewarded trial, higher after unrewarded (esp. S1); D2 common S1 low, S2 high
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 45 is dominated by timing (decays strongly over the episode, D2 > GO > D1; timing R^2 0.91). Beyond timing, the main driver is the last trial outcome: about -0.05 on all phases after a rewarded trial, plus about +0.03 more after an unrewarded trial that reached S1. At GO it is lower after a1->S2 unrewarded (rare-unrewarded, -0.04) and decreases slightly with the policy logit toward a1. At D2 it depends on this trial choice x state just observed: a1->S1 common about -0.056, a2->S2 common about +0.048. The reward two trials back adds a small negative effect (-0.008). Largest remaining misses are late-episode reward streaks where the unit is lower than predicted. Hidden good state, since-reversal and value add little. Only observed / model quantities are used. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.49 vs all ceiling 0.55 (about 89%).

issues: The scores reproduce. On --split test the terms give R^2 beyond timing 0.4907 against an 'all' ceiling of 0.55 (89%) and an all-observed ceiling of 0.52. Timing alone gives R^2 0.91.

The directional claims hold in the profile residual tables. After a rewarded trial residuals are about -0.02 to -0.06. After an unrewarded trial that reached S1 they are larger (D1 +0.07, GO +0.066/+0.096) than after one that reached S2 (D1 +0.045). At D2, a1->S1 is -0.058 and a2->S2 is +0.050. At GO after a1 S2 u the residual is -0.026.

The label overclaims a little. 'Higher after unrewarded' does not hold for a rare unrewarded trial (a1 S2 u) at GO (-0.026) or at D2 (-0.041). The explanation text covers this but the label does not. 'D2 common S1 low, S2 high' really means a1->S1 versus a2->S2; the rare-transition D2 cells (a2->S1 -0.014, a1->S2 +0.015) are not modelled.
The minor terms each add little. Dropping the GO choice logit (a model output) gives 0.468. Dropping reward two trials back gives 0.487. Dropping GO*a1 S2 u gives 0.485.
Misses with the original terms show some leftover error by previous trial, at most about 0.04: GO after a1 S2 r -0.039, D2 after a2 S1 u -0.035, D2 after a1 S2 u -0.030, D2 after a2 S1 r +0.022.

The worst-fit windows are all late in the episode (trials 85-95) during reward streaks, where actual values sit 0.1-0.3 below predicted. The history effects grow with episode time. Scaling the terms by (1+ep_trial/30) and adding GO*a1 S2 r raises test R^2 only to 0.51, so this is a scale effect and not a missing variable class. Plain reward-count or prev_reward*ep_trial interactions add under 0.006.
